name: EoL3D
title: Step-by-step teardowns of end-of-life desktop computers
tagline: Real desktop computers taken apart by hand and imaged from four views after every step, with instance masks, part states and removal order, plus question-answer pairs, operator video and robot demonstrations.
description: EoL3D is a dataset of 66 end-of-life desktop computers disassembled step by step: 2,748 steps, 11,221 images from four views, 84,225 instance annotations, 184,263 question-answer pairs, operator video and robot demonstrations.

download.use: Instance segmentation and detection on the scanner view, with part states and relations
Recognising parts outside the machine (the parts laid out after the teardown)
The scanner's 3D reconstructions, one labelled point cloud per step
Operator video of the hands at work, faces masked
Every capture of the four views, as the capture rigs wrote it
Robot demonstrations, one archive per episode, in two settings
Part classes, states and verbs; the train and test split

tasks.name: Visible component boxes
tasks.asks: Every part visible in one image, with its class and box.
tasks.scored: F1 over class-and-box matches at IoU 0.5 or more.

tasks.name: Component grounding
tasks.asks: The box of a part named in the question.
tasks.scored: Hit when the box overlaps the true box at IoU 0.5 or more.

tasks.name: Component state or screw count
tasks.asks: The state of a marked part, or "cannot tell" when the image does not show it; or how many screws of one kind are still in place.
tasks.scored: Exact match; a screw count that is off by one earns partial credit.

tasks.name: Same step across views
tasks.asks: Whether two images from two cameras show the same step.

tasks.name: Observed operation
tasks.asks: What was done between two moments: the operation and the part it was done to; asked without a hint, with a hint box, and over a span of steps.
tasks.scored: Correct when verb and target are both right; over a span, F1 over the action groups.

tasks.name: State change
tasks.asks: Whether anything changed between two moments, from neighbouring steps to several steps apart.

tasks.name: Completed operations
tasks.asks: Which operations have been carried out so far, and how far the teardown has got.
tasks.scored: F1 over the completed and started operations; accuracy of the progress bin.

tasks.name: Proposed action feasibility
tasks.asks: Whether an action on a marked part can be done now and, if not, which parts have to be dealt with first.
tasks.scored: Accuracy of the yes or no; F1 over the parts named as blocking.

tasks.name: Next feasible action
tasks.asks: Every action that can be done now; also as multiple choice, and under one added rule.
tasks.scored: F1 over the groups of feasible actions; accuracy for the multiple choice.

tasks.name: Removal plan
tasks.asks: A plan that takes a named part out, free or under one added rule.
tasks.scored: The plan is replayed on the relations: valid, goal reached, recall of the required steps.

tasks.name: Proposed plan validity
tasks.asks: Whether a proposed sequence of actions can be carried out, and the first step that cannot.
tasks.scored: Replayed step by step on the relations: accuracy of the validity and of the first wrong step.
